skill.name: set-up-shopify-meta-new-customer-bidding
skill.description: Use Product Metrics to connect first paid Shopify orders to Meta conversion events. Check tracking, review how orders are classified, and set up a custom conversion based on first-order revenue or profit.
skill.summary: Set up and verify first-order conversion tracking for Meta campaigns that aim to acquire Shopify customers.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most static flags match documentation or scoped Product Metrics operations, but the unpinned installer executes third-party code. The workflow also risks exposing Meta credentials and order details, enabling live event delivery without explicit approval, and selecting the wrong profit event. No evidence of malicious intent or direct prompt injection was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: The Meta access token can enter agent input and command arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Require token entry in the authenticated Product Metrics app or an approved secret field. Remove instructions to request the token or pass it as a command argument.

remediation.issue: Tracking writes can enable live delivery without explicit approval.
remediation.suggestion: Default to read-only mode. Confirm the Shopify store, Meta dataset, consent settings, and data fields before connecting a destination, enabling delivery, or leaving test mode.

remediation.issue: The setup check can expose detailed order and margin records.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the storefront and authorized order range before reading orders. Return classification counts by default and omit customer identifiers and margins unless needed.

remediation.issue: The main workflow names a general profit event for a first-order profit goal.
remediation.suggestion: Use PMNewCustomerProfit with CUSTOMER_NEW_PROFIT consistently. Tell the operator to verify the event and filter on a test order before changing an ad set.

remediation.issue: The optional installation example does not pin the executable package or skill revision.
remediation.suggestion: Document installation with a reviewed installer version and immutable skill revision. Keep installation separate from the runtime workflow.

remediation.issue: The fallback can load mutable instructions from public documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle versioned references. Treat remote copies as informational and check them against the reviewed revision before applying any changes.

semantic_findings.title: Meta Token Requested Through the Assistant
semantic_findings.description: The Meta guide says, "An assistant must ask you for it," despite recommending entry in the app. The skill instructs the assistant to pass the token directly to a command. This could expose a live credential in chat, tool arguments, or process listings.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both instructions explicitly allow the assistant to handle the token. They provide no protected input method for that route.

semantic_findings.title: Live Tracking Changes Lack an Explicit Approval Step
semantic_findings.description: The assistant can perform Product Metrics writes, but the rules require explicit approval only for deletes. The setup can enable Meta delivery and clear test mode. Those changes can start sending order events and customer matching data to the configured Meta dataset.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The references specify live delivery controls and the customer data sent with consent. The skill does not require separate approval before the assistant changes those controls.

semantic_findings.title: Order Checks Can Retrieve More Data Than Needed
semantic_findings.description: The reference asks for classifications of recent orders. The skill directs detailed order lookups that can expose margins to the assistant, even when classification counts would answer the question.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill explicitly says order details include margins. Neither instruction limits the lookup to classification fields or requires a redacted summary.

semantic_findings.title: Conflicting Profit Event Could Change Bidding Scope
semantic_findings.description: The main skill recommends PMOrderProfit for profit bidding, while the linked guide specifies PMNewCustomerProfit for first orders. Following the main instruction could make the campaign optimize for profit from repeat purchases as well.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The two files specify different event names and filters for profit bidding. The related guide scopes only PMNewCustomerProfit to first orders.

content.user_title: Set Up New Customer Bidding for Shopify in Meta
content.value_statement: A standard purchase event does not tell Meta whether a Shopify order came from a new customer. Use Product Metrics to verify first-order events and configure a Meta conversion for customer acquisition.
actual_capabilities: Check Product Metrics setup status through its CLI or MCP server to identify incomplete steps.
Guide the merchant through connecting a Shopify store and Meta dataset with Product Metrics.
Review recent Shopify orders and distinguish new, returning, and unknown customers.
Provide the event and filter for a first-order revenue or profit conversion in Meta Events Manager.
Guide a consented test order and verify that the expected event arrives in Meta.
limitations: Live tracking requires a connected Shopify store, an active Product Metrics subscription, and access to the correct Meta dataset.
The merchant creates the Meta custom conversion and selects the ad set optimization event.
Orders without a linked Shopify customer cannot count as first orders. Profit events also require complete margin data.
Past orders are not imported, and later refunds do not update events already sent to Meta.

use_cases.title: Check Store Readiness
use_cases.description: Find which Shopify and Meta setup steps are complete before creating a first-order conversion.

use_cases.title: Pilot a First-Order Bidding Signal
use_cases.description: Review the revenue and profit options, then configure one pilot ad set around a first-order custom conversion.

use_cases.title: Investigate Missing First-Order Events
use_cases.description: Check whether consent, test mode, order history, or incomplete costs explain a missing conversion event.

prompt_templates.title: Check Setup Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether my Shopify store and Meta dataset are connected in Product Metrics. Do not change any settings.

prompt_templates.title: Review Order Classifications
prompt_templates.prompt: Confirm the Shopify storefront first. Summarize my last 20 paid orders as new, returning, or unknown without showing customer details or margins.
prompt_templates.scenario: Before choosing a first-order conversion event.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Revenue Event Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Give me the steps to test a first-order revenue event with consent. Show where to verify it in Meta without changing live delivery or my ad set.
prompt_templates.scenario: When the Meta connection is ready for a test order.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate a Profit Pilot
prompt_templates.prompt: Review whether I can pilot first-order profit bidding on one ad set. Verify the event filter and cost readiness, and list changes for me to approve.
prompt_templates.scenario: When first-order revenue events already arrive in Meta.

output_examples.input: Check whether my store is ready to create a first-order revenue conversion.
output: Shopify is connected, and the Meta destination is saved.
A first-order revenue event has not appeared in Meta Test Events yet.
Place a paid test order using payment test mode and a new customer email. Accept marketing and analytics consent.

output_examples.input: Summarize the first-order classifications for my last 20 paid orders.
output: Six orders were new, 12 were returning, and two were unknown.
The two unknown orders had no linked Shopify customer. They do not count toward the first-order conversion.

best_practices: Enter the Meta token in the authenticated Product Metrics app. Keep it out of chat and command arguments.
Verify the destination and consent banner with a paid test order before approving live delivery.
Check that the event and filter match the first-order goal before selecting the conversion on one pilot ad set.
anti_patterns: Using a general purchase or order profit conversion when the goal is to bid on first orders.
Sharing customer details or order margins when classification counts are enough.
Leaving the test event code active when you expect events to count in live reporting.

faq.question: What access do I need?
faq.answer: You need Shopify permissions for the app and theme, access to the Product Metrics workspace, and access to the Meta dataset in Events Manager.

faq.question: How does Product Metrics identify a new customer?
faq.answer: Product Metrics checks earlier orders linked to the same Shopify customer. An order without a linked customer cannot qualify.

faq.question: Can I bid on first-order profit instead of revenue?
faq.answer: Yes. The first-order profit event requires complete margin data. Use PMNewCustomerProfit with the CUSTOMER_NEW_PROFIT filter, not the general order profit event.

faq.question: Why is the event missing from Meta Events Manager?
faq.answer: Meta must first receive the event. Place a test order for a new customer and accept both marketing and analytics consent.

faq.question: Will the assistant change what my ad set optimizes for?
faq.answer: No. You create the custom conversion in Meta Events Manager and select it as the optimization event in your ad set.

faq.question: Will old orders or refunds change the bidding signal?
faq.answer: No. Product Metrics does not import past orders, and Meta events already sent are not revised for later refunds.
